questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location (smaller city), academic reputation, language (already fluent in German).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of emails, which were confusing. I would have loved to get one common one with all the needed information. There did not seem to be cooperation between my home university and the host university. It took some energy to figure out, but not more than that. The secretary from the host university was confused and did not know which departments were at her university hospital - she placed me in a non-existent one.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some intro-days, but no particular information for medical students like for the others.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very difficult getting a student ID in order to get clothes at the hospital. A lot of bureaucracy...

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Facebook groups,
WG-gesucht.de

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I can recommend it, and look for accommodation well ahead of time, as you can not count on getting housing from the university..

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They first wrote me an email saying they could not offer me accommodation. Then, after I found private accommodation, they offered me one. I picked the private one, which also was a lot better and more central.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to submit which departments I wished for, and had to submit some vaccinations. Not that complicated. I did, however, find the online mobility and different platforms quite confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: From Copenhagen University, only emails. I asked to schedule phone calls, but this was unfortunately not possible.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the departments I wished for. However, infectiology did not exist as its own, even though it said to in the university folder. Instead, I was placed in gastroenterology. The secretary did not know this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can recommend taking a look at the university hospital's webpage to double check which departments actually exist.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I was only in clinical rotations, there was not really an academic programme. A shame that we can not take courses abroad from Copenhagen...

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations, 2. semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It seemed like a similar level, except for the fact that medical students in Germany have some different tasks than we do here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations in anaesthesiology, internal medicine, surgery.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anaesthesiology at Kopfklinik and the department of Visceral Surgery, because of very diverse surgeries, transplantations and anaesthetic procedures. European Pancreas Center is in Heidelberg.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Immatriculation fee of about 130 euros from the host university to get a Student ID, where you get free transportation on the weekend as well as after 7 pm on weekdays.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Things were generally more inexpensive than in Denmark. I can't think of anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of them begun in May, which was my last month.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different things. Both sports, and free concerts/cinema tickets as student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the castle, it is a small 10 minute hike and just enjoy the view. Bars in Untere Straße, chill at the Neckarwiese.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the whole beautiful region (Baden Württemberg) and surroundings. Take a lot of hikes. It is amazing and underappreciated.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy for me, but I knew about both cultural differences and the language from beforehand.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to the ESN-arranged intro weeks with hikes, pub-crawls, and so on. There you will meet other Erasmus students. Be in it from the beginning, otherwise it may be difficult to 'become part of a group'. Especially if you do not participate in the German course!

About German students: As we do not take courses, it is close to impossible to socialise with local students. At every hospital department there were German PJ students (who were in their last year of med school), and I personally hung out with them, went to their afternoon teachings and ate lunch with them and their friends. 
I can also recommend signing up for the buddy programme, as my buddy introduced me to arrangements with other local students as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hierarchy in the hospital, where there for example is a Chefarzt who no one dares speak up to. It was difficult getting used to saying 'Sie' instead of 'du' to all the doctors. It is a fine balance.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Effectiveness, focus on learning.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Double check the departments, look for accommodation well in advance, but most of all go and enjoy it. (be prepared to take a lot of blood samples and put in iv's - those are medical student's tasks in Germany. Not necessary to be able to do it in advance, but be prepared to learn it)
Also - do NOT expect that the departments know you are coming or will be waiting for you. They most likely will not know, and you have to introduce yourself and take a lot of initiative. Only the secretary knows you are coming.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes, what I wrote above. And get your student ID as soon as possible. Expect a lot of bureaucracy from both Copenhagen University as well as Heidelberg University.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just living in the gorgeous city, visiting the region, meeting great people, making connections in the hospital, assisting and doing a lot of procedures I would not be able to here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bureaucracy - getting clothes, student ID, and so on. 
Also adapting to the culture, differences in tasks as a medical student here and there.
Making sure my 'log-bog' was signed, which the students in Copenhagen do not need to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can only recommend, but sad to leave before all the other students who actually take courses that last until the end of July. It would have been nice to have a full semester instead of only 3 months.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
